hints.title: Three-Stage Interval Partition
hints.text: The input intervals are already sorted without overlap. Partition the process into intervals completely before newInterval, overlapping intervals, and intervals after.

hints.title: Dynamic Overlap Merging
hints.text: While the current interval overlaps with newInterval, expand newInterval start to min of starts and newInterval end to max of ends.

hints.title: Linear Pass Combination
hints.text: Append all intervals ending before newInterval starts. Next merge all overlapping intervals into one merged interval. Finally append the merged interval and all remaining intervals.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def insert(self, intervals: List[List[int]], newInterval: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
        res = []
        i, n = 0, len(intervals)
        while i < n and intervals[i][1] < newInterval[0]:
            res.append(intervals[i])
            i += 1
        while i < n and intervals[i][0] <= newInterval[1]:
            newInterval[0] = min(newInterval[0], intervals[i][0])
            newInterval[1] = max(newInterval[1], intervals[i][1])
            i += 1
        res.append(newInterval)
        while i < n:
            res.append(intervals[i])
            i += 1
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Appending newInterval and re-sorting the whole array takes O(N log N) time, ignoring the pre-sorted property.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single linear scan collects non-overlapping prefix, merged overlap, and remaining suffix in O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should take advantage of pre-sorted order and merge in a single linear pass without re-sorting.
